claims.claim: A bank is a financial intermediary that takes deposits from savers and lends to borrowers, standing between the two.
On a bank's balance sheet, assets include reserves, loans, and bonds, while deposits are liabilities; net worth (bank capital) equals assets minus liabilities.
Under fractional-reserve banking a bank holds only a fraction of deposits as reserves and lends the rest, and the banking system creates money as loans become new deposits.

The simple money multiplier equals 1 divided by the reserve ratio; with a $10 million deposit and a 10 percent reserve ratio the multiplier is 10 and about $90 million in new money can be created, total deposits reaching $100 million.
The real-world money multiplier is smaller than the simple version because people hold cash outside banks and banks hold excess reserves, both of which interrupt the re-deposit chain.

A bank run occurs when depositors, fearing the bank has or will have negative net worth, rush to withdraw; because reserves are fractional, even a solvent bank can be forced to close, and the fear can be self-fulfilling.
Deposit insurance repays depositors even if their bank fails, removing the incentive to run; the FDIC was created in 1933.
Standard FDIC deposit insurance coverage is $250,000 per depositor, per insured bank, per ownership category.
The $250,000 standard maximum deposit insurance amount was made permanent by the Dodd-Frank Act, effective July 22, 2010 (retroactive to January 1, 2008).

sourceRecords.title: Principles of Macroeconomics 3e, 14.3 The Role of Banks
sourceRecords.notes: Supports banks as financial intermediaries and the balance-sheet structure (assets: reserves, loans, bonds; liabilities: deposits; net worth = bank capital). Read via WebFetch; NonCommercial license, so facts synthesized and prose written originally.

sourceRecords.title: Principles of Macroeconomics 3e, 14.4 How Banks Create Money
sourceRecords.notes: Supports fractional-reserve money creation, the Singleton Bank example ($10M deposit, 10% reserve, $9M lent), the money multiplier = 1/reserve requirement (10x $9M = $90M), and leakages (cash held outside banks, excess reserves). Arithmetic independently verified in Bash.

sourceRecords.title: Principles of Macroeconomics 3e, 15.2 Bank Regulation
sourceRecords.notes: Supports the definition of a bank run (fear of negative net worth, self-fulfilling), why fractional reserves make even solvent banks vulnerable, and deposit insurance / lender of last resort as the two safeguards. Lender-of-last-resort detail handed off to the federal-reserve topic.
